articles.title: The Forbidden City: Inside China's largest imperial palace complex, a hidden empire within a city for 500 years | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: The Forbidden City, a palace complex in Beijing, was built during the Ming dynasty to project imperial power and reflect its political structure.  Its layout, influenced by Chinese philosophical traditions, organized hierarchy through architectural features like building size and placement. The public side of the complex housed government ceremonies and served as a stage for state rituals, while the northern section functioned as the residence of the imperial household, reflecting traditional family roles.  The palace's history includes alterations made under Empress Dowager Cixi and later transformed into a museum after the fall of the Qing dynasty. The Forbidden City now serves as a place to learn about China's imperial past and is constantly being preserved and interpreted for public access.

articles.title: Relax, it will all work out, says Trump, as Iran hangs up - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Iran suspended communications with the US after accusing Israel of violating a ceasefire in Lebanon, escalating tensions that have seen both sides report fresh military strikes.  Oil markets reacted with alarm to the prospect of renewed conflict, while international leaders urged de-escalation and called for dialogue between the two nations. The situation mirrors a familiar pattern of diplomacy by day and missiles by night, raising concerns about global economic stability and security.

articles.title: Timeline of Henry Nowak murder case: Southampton's Vickram Digwa who killed 18-year-old student with Sikh dagger sentenced for life - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Vickrum Digwa, 22, was sentenced to life imprisonment for the murder of Henry Nowak, an 18-year-old finance student in Southampton, UK.  Digwa stabbed Nowak five times with a religious knife, claiming racial abuse as justification. The incident occurred on December 3, 2025, and sparked national attention due to the police's initial handcuffing of Nowak before realizing he was fatally wounded. The Sikh Federation criticized the Crown Prosecution Service for its handling of the case, while the judge condemned Digwa's actions as causing racial tension in Southampton and beyond.

articles.title: Asylum rejections without interviews? Trump administration moves to speed up deportation cases under new plan - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: The Trump administration is proposing a new immigration policy that would allow US Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) officers to deny asylum applications without interviewing applicants if they believe the claims were filed more than a year after entry. This change, developed by the Department of Homeland Security (DHS), aims to address a growing backlog of asylum cases but has raised concerns among immigration advocates who worry it could lead to people being deported without proper explanation for delays in filing their claims. The proposal would still allow officers to move cases forward for interview if they believe an exception applies, but the key change is that officers would be able to rely on paperwork alone to dismiss cases outside the legal time limit.

articles.title: 'Plume of smoke': At least two injured after fireworks factory explosion rattles northern Malta - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: A series of explosions at a fireworks factory in Malta injured two men working nearby. The initial blast occurred around 6:35 am local time, followed by several smaller explosions. Edward Mercieca, a resident, described feeling the force of the first explosion like a truck-sized hammer striking his house.  Prime Minister Robert Abela expressed condolences and confirmed authorities were dispatched to provide assistance.

articles.title: Longest solar eclipse of the century: The 6-minute 23-second total eclipse will darken the daytime sky | - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: The longest total solar eclipse of the 21st century will occur on August 2, 2027, visible in parts of Spain, Morocco, Algeria, Libya, Egypt, and Saudi Arabia.  Fred Espenak, a scientist quoted on NASA's website, attributes this long duration to the alignment of the Earth, moon, and sun at their respective positions. The eclipse will last approximately six minutes and 23 seconds, offering viewers a spectacular view of the solar corona and other rare astronomical phenomena. NASA advises viewers to use certified solar viewing glasses to safely observe the event.

articles.title: Trump says Iran talks continue 'at rapid pace' as Tehran suspends negotiations after Lebanon strikes - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: President Donald Trump stated that negotiations with Iran are continuing at a rapid pace despite recent exchanges of fire between the two sides. Trump also spoke with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and representatives of Hezbollah, assuring that no troops would be sent to Beirut and that Hezbollah had agreed to halt attacks on Israel. However, Trump acknowledged that he hadn't been formally informed of Iran's reported decision to suspend negotiations, but stated the US wouldn't initiate an attack. The developments come amidst escalating tensions in Lebanon as Israel continues its military campaign there.

articles.title: 87-year-old Florida man dies after Tesla on Autopilot mode crashes into pond - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: An 87-year-old man driving a Tesla Model Y died after his vehicle crashed into an electrical box and submerged in a pond while operating in Autopilot mode near Tampa. The incident occurred last month, and the Florida Highway Patrol is investigating the cause of the crash.  The driver's passenger, a 75-year-old woman, sustained non-life-threatening injuries. Tesla CEO Elon Musk has previously expressed confidence in the future of autonomous driving technology, but this fatal accident highlights ongoing concerns about the safety and reliability of Autopilot. The investigation is ongoing.

articles.title: Discoms' poor financial health poses risks for power traders: Fitch - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Fitch Ratings warns that the financial struggles of state electricity boards in India pose a significant risk to power traders.  The agency cites widening losses and liquidity constraints at these utilities, leading to delays and defaults in payments to traders. This increased counterparty risk could force investors to seek higher returns or alternative investments, potentially impacting the business of power trading companies like PTC India and Tata Power Trading Company. The report highlights that states with significant short-term electricity purchases from traders, such as Tamil Nadu and Rajasthan, face substantial energy deficits and financial losses.

articles.title: Myanmar explosion toll rises to 55. What we know so far | World News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: An explosion at a warehouse storing industrial explosives in Kaungtup village, Myanmar, on Sunday, May 31, 2026, killed at least 55 people and injured over 100. The Ta’ang National Liberation Army (TNLA), which controls the area, classified the incident as an accidental explosion.  The blast destroyed or damaged approximately 200 homes in Kaungtup village and a further 100 homes in Pan Lone. Survivors expressed anger and demanded accountability from authorities over lax safety standards that allowed the explosives to be stored so close to residential areas.

articles.title: Ashok Vada Pav ranks 25th in TasteAtlas' Most Iconic Sandwiches List
articles.rephrased_article: TasteAtlas, a popular food guide, ranked Mumbai's Ashok Vada Pav 25th in its list of The World’s Most Iconic Sandwiches.  The snack, believed to have been invented by street vendor Ashok Vaidya in the 1960s or 70s, is an iconic street food staple in Mumbai, known for its affordability and convenience. Celebrity chef Ananya Banerjee highlighted the dish's cultural significance as a symbol of Mumbai's industrious spirit.  Tarveen Kaur, head chef and restaurant consultant, agreed that vada pav represents the essence of Mumbai, a simple yet profound snack with enduring popularity across India.

articles.title: ROG turns 20: ASUS introduces G1000 Edition 20, Xbox Ally X20, and outlines AI future | Technology News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: ASUS ROG celebrated its 20th anniversary with a special event in Taipei, Taiwan.  The company unveiled the Edition 20 collection, a limited-edition lineup of gaming PCs, components, peripherals, lifestyle products, and software. ASUS Chairman Jonney Shih highlighted the future of gaming, where AI could enable gamers to create entire worlds on their own. The anniversary also saw collaborations with industry partners like AMD, Intel, Microsoft, and NVIDIA.  The event featured new hardware such as the ROG G1000 Edition 20 desktop, Anniversary editions of components, and a board game based on the ROG Saga universe.  Kris Huang, general manager of gaming and workspace gear business unit at Asus, spoke about the brand's early days and its evolution into an ecosystem. ASUS plans to continue focusing on innovation in gaming and AI-powered features.

articles.title: Man Stuck In 120-Metre Italian Cave Saved By 53 Rescuers
articles.rephrased_article: A caver trapped at a depth of 120 meters in the Grotta dei Cinghiali Volanti cave in Italy was successfully rescued overnight.  Fifty-three people, including members of the Alpine and Speleological Rescue Service, participated in the operation. The caver was transported to a hospital by ambulance after being initially treated at a makeshift medical post within the cave.

articles.title: Best Sleep Trackers of 2026: Oura, Whoop, and Eight Sleep | WIRED
articles.rephrased_article: Sleep trackers are evolving from passive tracking to active guidance, offering personalized insights.  Oura Ring, Whoop, and Eight Sleep Pod 5 stand out for their accuracy and comprehensive data. Wearable options like the Google Pixel Watch 4 and Apple Watch Series 11 provide basic sleep monitoring, while Garmin Epix Pro offers advanced sleep analysis.  The Withings Sleep Tracking Mat and Sleep Routine app offer alternative approaches. While wearables can increase awareness of sleep patterns, excessive reliance on data may lead to stress or inaccurate interpretations. It's crucial to prioritize internal cues over external metrics for optimal sleep.

articles.title: Lactose Intolerance Patches Enter the Market, But Do They Really Work?
articles.rephrased_article: A new company has launched wearable transdermal lactose relief patches, claiming to help people enjoy dairy products without experiencing symptoms. Dr Aravinda S N, Lead Consultant – Internal Medicine at Aster RV Hospital, Bangalore, cautions that while some users report feeling better, there is limited scientific evidence supporting the effectiveness of these patches. He also notes that they may not be suitable for individuals with severe lactose intolerance or sensitive skin and emphasizes the importance of consulting a healthcare professional before using them.

articles.title: 80-Kg Dummy, Missing Belt: Cops Check Forensic Details In Twisha Sharma Case
articles.rephrased_article: The CBI recreated the events surrounding actress-model Twisha Sharma's death using an 80-kilogram dummy suspended from a noose. The agency is attempting to verify the claims made by accused husband Samarth Singh and his mother, former judge Giribala Singh, about how Twisha died.  The investigation also involves examining medical records, witness statements, digital evidence, and allegations of assault before her death. CBI officials are analyzing mobile phone data, call records, banking transactions, location history, and digital chats to track Samarth Singh's movements after the FIR was registered and identify those who may have helped him evade arrest.  The agency is also investigating the alleged mishandling of evidence, including the ligature belt, which was not immediately deposited as evidence.

articles.title: US stocks today: US stocks end higher, boosted by tech gains, US-Iran peace hopes - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The Nasdaq and S&P 500 reached record closing highs, boosted by tech shares and positive developments in the US-Iran conflict.  President Donald Trump stated that no Israeli troops would enter Beirut, while Nvidia unveiled a new AI chip, driving gains for the company and semiconductor stocks. However, concerns over inflation linked to the ongoing war in Iran and geopolitical tensions persisted. The Philadelphia SE Semiconductor Index advanced, but some semiconductor companies like Qualcomm saw declines.  The US factory activity expanded for the fifth consecutive month, while investors await Friday's jobs report and Kevin Warsh's debut as chairman of the U.S. Federal Reserve.

articles.title: Iran Threatens "New Fronts" In War As Peace Talk Cliffhanger Continues
articles.rephrased_article: Iran's Revolutionary Guards have threatened to open new fronts in the conflict after Israel expanded its offensive in Lebanon, suspending dialogue with mediators. The latest escalation of violence coincides with weeks of indirect talks that have failed to reach an agreement on ending the war or reopening the Strait of Hormuz.  The US has backed Israel's operations while still attempting to negotiate a deal with Iran to end the conflict and reopen the Strait of Hormuz, but Iran insists Israel must halt its offensive in Lebanon before any wider agreement can be reached. The UN Security Council is holding an emergency meeting on Lebanon amid escalating tensions.

articles.title: Anthropic Confidentially Files for What Could Be the Largest IPO Ever | WIRED
articles.rephrased_article: Anthropic, a leading artificial intelligence lab, submitted confidential paperwork for an initial public offering (IPO) on Monday. The filing with the US Securities and Exchange Commission is the first step in what could be a historic year for IPOs as AI labs seek funding to support their research. Anthropic, led by CEO Dario Amodei, joins other companies like OpenAI and SpaceX that are also pursuing public offerings. The company's IPO preparations involve addressing accounting, internal policies, and investor pitches, potentially leading to significant wealth creation for employees and large shareholders.  However, Anthropic's complex corporate structure and its ethical stance on AI use could impact the IPO process.

articles.title: AI giant Anthropic files for US IPO as investors bet big on AI future | Technology News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Anthropic, the AI chatbot developer behind Claude, filed for a US IPO. This move comes as investors seek to capitalize on the burgeoning AI market and follows in the footsteps of other tech giants like SpaceX.  The company's rapid growth has led some analysts to believe that it could surpass rival OpenAI in valuation, potentially disrupting traditional business models and reshaping the stock market landscape.

articles.title: Kenyans protest planned US Ebola quarantine facility | Ebola News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Hundreds of Kenyans protested near a military base in Nanyuki, Kenya, against the planned US Ebola quarantine facility. The protest followed a court order suspending the plan and sparked anger over concerns about public health and transparency. US officials say the 50-bed unit would serve asymptomatic Americans exposed to the virus but have not released detailed plans for the facility.  The protesters demand the facility be shut down, citing potential risks to their community's health and safety.

articles.title: Hasan Piker and Cenk Uygur blocked from entering UK by Home Office
articles.rephrased_article: Two US political commentators, Hasan Piker and Cenk Uygur, were denied entry to the United Kingdom by the Home Office after they criticized Israel. The pair had been scheduled to speak at SXSW London and an event in Oxford.  The Home Office has not commented on the decision but Labour MP David Taylor praised the move, stating that it prevents individuals who spread hate and division from entering the country. Piker and Uygur have a history of controversial comments, including statements about Hamas and Israel, which some groups have criticized as antisemitic.

articles.title: Amid Public Fury, Trinamool Leaders Return 'Cut Money' In Bengal Village
articles.rephrased_article: In Cooch Behar's Mathabhanga district, Trinamool Congress leaders and workers are returning money they collected as "cut money" or through extortion. The unprecedented incident took place on Sunday in the Fakirer Kuthi area of Pachagarh Gram Panchayat, where villagers were called to a gathering.  Tapan Dey, the TMC booth president, personally handed back some of the money to several villagers. Babai Barman, a highly influential Trinamool leader who is currently on the run, has also been forced to return some funds.

articles.title: Italians bemused by Milan bull mosaic restoration
articles.rephrased_article: Italian city council officials have restored a famous bull mosaic in Milan's Galleria Vittorio Emanuele II arcade, sparking online debate about the removal of the bull's testicles. The restoration project was undertaken to repair a crater formed by tourists grinding their heels on the bull's private parts, but some users expressed confusion and concern over the apparent loss of the animal's "lucky-charm" feature.  The council stated that the restoration is not yet complete and that the work is being carried out under the watchful eye of officials, adding that no testicles have been removed.

articles.title: Former election clerk Tina Peters released after Trump pressure campaign | Donald Trump News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Tina Peters, a former Colorado election clerk convicted of tampering with voting machines, was released from prison after pressure from Donald Trump.  Colorado's Secretary of State Jena Griswold expressed opposition to her release, stating it sends a dangerous message about accountability. Peters, a Trump supporter who was part of an election denial movement, had been sentenced to nine years in state prison but received clemency from Colorado Governor Jared Polis. Critics argue that Peters' lack of remorse and continued spread of false claims about election fraud are concerning.

articles.title: Serena Williams to return to tennis at Queen's Club - BBC Sport
articles.rephrased_article: Serena Williams, a 44-year-old former tennis champion, will return to competitive action in the women's doubles at Queen's Club later this month.  She has been granted a wildcard and will play alongside Canadian teenager Victoria Mboko. Williams announced her return after being included on the International Tennis Integrity Agency (ITIA) reinstatements list. She last competed at the 2022 US Open, retiring in 2022 after winning 23 Grand Slam singles titles.

articles.title: Trump halts $1.8bn ‘anti-weaponisation’ fund amid bipartisan backlash | Politics News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump announced the suspension of his $1.8 billion “anti-weaponisation” fund amid bipartisan backlash from congressional Republicans and Democrats. The fund, part of a settlement between Trump and the Internal Revenue Service (IRS), was intended to compensate victims of "lawfare" and government "weaponization."  Republican leaders like Mike Johnson, John Thune, and Chuck Schumer have called for its discontinuation, citing concerns about potential conflicts of interest and misuse. The fund faced legal challenges from groups like Democracy Forward and Citizens for Responsibility and Ethics in Washington (CREW) who argued it lacked legal authority and was a tool for payouts to Trump supporters.  Despite the White House's statement that it would comply with court rulings to pause the fund, Senate Republicans signaled their support for the $72 billion immigration enforcement funding bill, which had been delayed due to the controversy.

articles.title: Florida Sues OpenAI, Sam Altman Over ChatGPT Safety Risks
articles.rephrased_article: Florida's attorney general, James Uthmeier, filed a lawsuit against OpenAI and its CEO, Sam Altman, alleging that the company's ChatGPT chatbot endangers young users by promoting addiction and harmful behaviors. The suit cites a study from Drexel University showing negative effects on teenagers who use chatbots for conversation, including sleep loss and declining grades. Uthmeier also points to a report from the Center for Countering Digital Hate (CCDH) that revealed ChatGPT providing advice on hiding eating habits and planning suicide or self-harm.  The lawsuit seeks stronger protections for minors and damages of $10,000 per violation.

articles.title: Hungarian PM threatens to oust Orbán-era president
articles.rephrased_article: Péter Magyar, Hungary's new prime minister, has threatened to remove Tamás Sulyok, the president appointed by his predecessor Viktor Orbán.  Magyar claims Sulyok serves Orbán's interests and accuses him of not upholding the rule of law. Sulyok, who was installed in February 2024, refuses to resign and has stated that he will complete his term. The stand-off between the new government and the president is creating a constitutional clash with potential consequences for Hungary's EU funding.

articles.title: Armenian PM rejects Russia’s demand for EU referendum as relations nosedive | Vladimir Putin News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Nikol Pashinyan, the Armenian Prime Minister, rejected a demand from Vladimir Putin, the Russian President, to hold an immediate referendum on leaving the Eurasian Economic Union (EAEU) to join the European Union.  The Kremlin has been increasing pressure on Armenia ahead of parliamentary elections in June, including recalling its ambassador and imposing trade restrictions. Pashinyan stated that Armenia will continue working within the EAEU until a choice between the two blocs becomes unavoidable, calling the Russian demand "unreasonable." The Armenian government is diversifying its partnerships as it seeks closer ties with the European Union following Russia's invasion of Ukraine.

articles.title: OpenAI let ChatGPT aid and abet mass shooters, Florida suit says
articles.rephrased_article: Florida Attorney General James Uthmeier filed a lawsuit against OpenAI, alleging the company's AI chatbot, ChatGPT, endangers children, aids and abets mass shooters, and encourages suicide. The lawsuit claims Sam Altman, OpenAI's CEO, is personally liable for reckless conduct.  The suit cites the Florida State University mass shooting and the killing of two University of South Florida doctoral students as examples of ChatGPT's harmful potential. OpenAI responded by stating it prioritizes safety and has implemented industry-leading protections for minors.

articles.title: Protesters call on Kenyan government to halt femicide crisis | Women's Rights News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Thousands of Kenyans, mostly women, marched through central Nairobi on Monday to demand the government declare a national crisis over rising cases of femicide and child disappearances.  The protest, organized by End Femicide, alongside other advocacy groups, was spurred by the brutal murder of gospel singer Rachel Wandeto who was doused with petrol and set on fire in May. The group gave the Kenyan government 40 days to intervene or face nationwide protests.  Former Chief Justice David Maraga joined the march lending his voice to calls for stronger government action. The Federation of Women Lawyers in Kenya reports receiving roughly 70 gender-based violence cases every week and over 10,500 child protection cases were recorded between January 2025 and March 2026.

articles.title: Is the US-backed Gaza peace process in serious danger? | Israel-Palestine conflict | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Israel continues to attack Palestinians in Gaza, violating the October ceasefire agreement and resulting in over 900 deaths.  Experts on the program discuss whether this escalation poses a serious threat to the US-backed peace process.  Muhammad Shehada, Daniel Levy, and Tamer Qarmout offer their insights into the current situation.

articles.title: Hezbollah Accepts US Proposal For Mutual Halt To Attacks With Israel
articles.rephrased_article: Hezbollah has agreed to a US proposal for a mutual cessation of hostilities that would extend to encompass all Lebanese territory. Israel has agreed to refrain from striking Beirut's southern suburbs in exchange for Hezbollah halting its attacks against Israel, according to the Lebanese embassy in Washington.  The arrangement is contingent on a full ceasefire across Lebanon and the withdrawal of Israeli troops.

articles.title: Lactose Intolerance Patches Enter the Market, But Do They Really Work?
articles.rephrased_article: A new company has launched wearable transdermal lactose relief patches, claiming to help people enjoy dairy products without experiencing symptoms.  Dr Aravinda S N, Lead Consultant – Internal Medicine at Aster RV Hospital, Bangalore, cautions that while some users report feeling better, there is limited scientific evidence supporting the effectiveness of these patches and they may not be suitable for everyone. Dr Aravinda suggests consulting a healthcare professional before using them and emphasizes that they are not a substitute for proven treatments like lactase enzyme supplements or dietary changes.

articles.title: Who was Dave Fiji? Indian-origin pilot killed in helicopter crash in Georgia hours after marrying long-time partner - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Dave Fiji, an Indian-origin pilot with Delta Air Lines, was killed in a helicopter crash near Dawsonville, Georgia, shortly after his wedding ceremony. The couple boarded the Robinson R66 helicopter for a post-wedding send-off and the aircraft crashed during takeoff, killing both the pilot and Fiji.  Jesni, Fiji's long-time partner, survived the crash with injuries and is recovering in hospital. The US National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) is investigating the accident.

articles.title: Trump needs this war to end but Iran is not backing down
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump and Iran are engaged in a tense standoff, with neither side willing to return to war despite the ceasefire.  The US maintains its military presence near Iran while Iran continues to assert its resolve and demands concessions for reopening the Strait of Hormuz. The situation is further complicated by disagreements within the US government regarding potential concessions to Iran. Qatar, Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates (UAE) are all working towards a diplomatic solution, but progress remains elusive.  The ongoing tension has significant global economic implications.

articles.title: The silken voice of Hindi cinema falls silent - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Suman Kalyanpur, a renowned singer, passed away in Mumbai on May 31, 2026, after a brief illness.  Born in Dhaka in 1937, she began her career singing Noor Jehan songs and later gained recognition for her collaborations with legendary musicians like Mohd Rafi and Talat Mahmood. Her soft-spoken nature and understated expressions made her voice unique, earning her comparisons to Lata Mangeshkar, but ultimately establishing a distinct style that resonated across generations.  Kalyanpur's legacy is marked by her contributions to Hindi film music, particularly in the golden age of the industry, where she sang in around 100 films and became known for her intimate vocal delivery and emotional depth.

articles.title: Iran warns Israeli attacks in Lebanon threaten ceasefire with US
articles.rephrased_article: Iran has warned that Israeli attacks against Hezbollah in Lebanon could threaten the ceasefire agreement with the US.  Abbas Araghchi, Iran's foreign minister, stated that any violation of the ceasefire would affect all fronts. Donald Trump confirmed ongoing talks with both Israel and Hezbollah, while Netanyahu insisted on Israeli strikes against Hezbollah targets in response to attacks. The Lebanese president's office reported Hezbollah's acceptance of a US proposal for a mutual cessation of attacks, but tensions remain high between the US and Iran.  The ceasefire agreement, which came into force on April 8th, has failed to end the fighting.

articles.title: Kaynes shares plunge 43% from October peak. Is a tactical rebound on the cards or more pain ahead? - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Anand James, Chief Market Strategist at Geojit Investments Limited, suggests a potential short-term downward trend in the Nifty, with support levels around 26,085–26,065.  The IT sector is expected to continue its upward momentum, potentially reaching 39,500, while PSU banks may experience a pullback early next week. COFORGE and ABCAPITAL are recommended as potential buy opportunities with targets of 2,080-2180 and 368-377 respectively.

articles.title: FPIs pull out Rs 27,000 cr in May; 2026 outflows hit Rs 2.2 lakh cr-mark - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Foreign Portfolio Investors (FPIs) have withdrawn a record Rs 2.2 lakh crore from the Indian equity market in 2026, exceeding the total outflows of Rs 1.66 lakh crore in 2025.  Himanshu Srivastava, Principal - Manager Research at Morningstar Investment Research India, attributed this trend to global growth uncertainty, geopolitical tensions, and volatility in crude oil prices, which have dampened risk appetite towards emerging markets. V K Vijayakumar, Chief Investment Strategist at Geojit Investments, highlighted the impact of sustained FPI selling on the rupee's depreciation, potentially reaching 96 to the US dollar.  He also noted that capital flows into AI-focused companies are diverting funds away from India.

articles.title: There is a leadership vacuum in Infosys, time to get Nandan Nilekani back: Mohandas Pai - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Mohandas Pai, former Infosys Board Member, believes the recent high-profile exits are a result of leadership vacuum and poor chemistry within the company. He suggests that the board needs to address this issue by appointing a new CEO with experience in enterprise management and fostering a strong connection between Nandan Nilekani, the executive chairman, and the next generation of leaders.  Pai also believes that some bloodletting is necessary for the company's future success and that external expertise may be needed.

articles.title: Our commitment for press freedom, and autonomy of public broadcast is absolute: Prakash Javadekar - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The Minister of state (independent charge) for information and broadcasting, environment and climate change, Prakash Javadekar, has outlined the government's approach to communication and media. The new I&B ministry will establish a social media hub to manage all ministers' social media outreach, including Facebook, Twitter, and other platforms.  The ministry aims to enhance transparency, effectiveness, and accessibility within the government's communications strategy.  Javadekar also emphasized the importance of public broadcaster autonomy while addressing concerns about potential media control. He highlighted the need for synergy between ministries and a focus on learning from the new government's approach to communication.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Centralized control of ministers' social media raises concerns about censorship and propaganda.

articles.title: Confidence level of industry improving: KV Kamath, ICICI Bank - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: KV Kamath, Chairman of ICICI Bank, believes the Indian economy will see growth in the first term of the current government. He anticipates a fiscal discipline approach in the upcoming budget and sees corporate investment picking up within three to six months. Kamath also expects a positive impact from reforms addressing stalled projects and monetary policy adjustments driven by fiscal discipline.  He predicts that interest rates could begin to decline within the next 12 months, potentially starting with a quarter percentage point reduction in the first half of the year.

articles.title: Narendra Modi has his eyes set on boosting business: Joao Cravinho, EU Ambassador - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Ambassador Joao Cravinho, head of the European Union delegation in India, met with Narendra Modi during his time as Gujarat Chief Minister.  He believes that the new Prime Minister has a clear vision for India and governance, and that EU member states have the potential to drive economic growth in India. The EU is already the largest trading partner and source of foreign direct investment for India. Cravinho expressed confidence that the FTA negotiations will benefit India and hopes for progress before the next India-EU Summit at Brussels.

articles.title: Every decision of government needn’t be a big reform: Anand Mahindra - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Anand Mahindra, chairman and MD of Mahindra & Mahindra, expressed optimism about the new Indian government's 10-point agenda, particularly its focus on empowering bureaucrats. He believes this will address bureaucratic paralysis and create a more inclusive economy.  Narendra Modi's leadership has been lauded by business leaders for his clear vision and commitment to economic growth. Mahindra & Mahindra remains committed to investing in India despite economic downturns, citing the company's long-term perspective on the market. The company is also confident in its ability to capitalize on opportunities in defense and infrastructure development.  The US administration is urged to rebuild a strong relationship with India as it seeks to enhance its global role.

articles.title: Documents reveal contents of the first telegraph message between India & England - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Newly discovered documents reveal the first telegraph messages sent from Porthcurno, England to Mumbai on June 23, 1870, marking a technological breakthrough in communication between Britain and its former colonies.  The Managing Director in London and the Manager in Bombay exchanged messages via undersea cables laid by the British Indian Submarine Telegraph Company. The first message was "How are you all?", which received a reply of "All well". This marked the beginning of a revolution that connected the world through telegraphy, with Porthcurno serving as a hub for international cable communications from 1870 to 1970 and later becoming a training college for the communications industry.  The museum, now housing rare equipment and details of the history of telegraph, has received millions in funding to develop an international education program that includes community groups in India.

articles.title: Kenya Protest: 'This will expose our people to Ebola': Big protest in Kenya against quarantine centre for affected US citizens - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Hundreds of youths protested in Nanyuki, Kenya, against plans to establish an Ebola quarantine center at Laikipia Air Base. The demonstration followed a court order suspending the facility's establishment and halting the arrival of foreign patients pending a case filed by local legal groups. Kenya’s Health Minister Aden Duale stated the center was intended for everyone, not exclusively US nationals, while US Secretary of State Marco Rubio pledged $13.5 million in support.  Local leaders, including Laikipia Governor Joshua Irungu, voiced opposition to the facility due to potential exposure risks to local residents.

articles.title: Delhi HC recognises ‘right to be forgotten’, lays down framework for de-indexing judicial records - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Delhi High Court ruled that the "right to be forgotten" exists under Article 21 of the Indian Constitution, granting individuals the right to have personal information removed from public digital accessibility. The court established a framework for de-indexing judicial records and masking personal identifiers from publicly accessible court records, ruling that such information should not indefinitely link individuals to past legal proceedings, especially when they are acquitted or proceedings have ended.  The court emphasized the importance of open justice while acknowledging exceptions in cases involving convictions for serious offenses.

articles.title: Jill Biden says she was shocked after Kamala Harris lost to Trump, 'You were?' asks interviewer - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Jill Biden stated in a new interview that she was certain Kamala Harris would win the 2024 election and beat Donald Trump, but was shocked when it did not happen. In her memoir, "Views from the East Wing," released tomorrow, Biden describes witnessing President Joe Biden's struggles during the presidential debate and expressing concerns about his health. She also recounts leaving notes for her husband, including encouraging messages and critiques of foreign policy decisions.

articles.title: Delhi World Book fair: A fair like no other - The Economic Times

Super 98 petrol now costs Dh3.95 per litre, up from Dh3.66 in May, while Special 95 and E-Plus 91 have also increased. Vijay Valecha, Chief Investment Officer at Century Financial, stated that physical oil markets remain tight due to shipping restrictions and broader regional security concerns.  The increase comes shortly after the UAE's historic decision to leave OPEC and OPEC+. Analysts are closely watching how future production policies could influence oil markets.

articles.title: Explained: NSE extends F&O trading by 10 minutes. What changes for traders? - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The National Stock Exchange of India (NSE) is extending the closing time for equity derivatives trading by 10 minutes to 3:40 pm, starting August 3, 2026. This change will be accompanied by a shift from a "continuous trading close" to an "auction discovered close," with a 20-minute auction session running from 3:15 pm to 3:35 pm for securities eligible for the CAS (Closing Auction Session). The new framework aims to ensure smoother transitions between cash and derivatives markets while maintaining consistency in pricing across segments.  The closing price of eligible securities will be determined through an auction process, with existing methodologies for calculating closing prices remaining unchanged for non-eligible securities.

articles.title: London tube strikes set to go ahead unless last-ditch talks deliver breakthrough | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Transport for London (TfL) and the National Union of Rail, Maritime and Transport Workers (RMT) are locked in a dispute over pay, working conditions, and staffing levels.  Union officials say workers deserve fair compensation amid rising living costs, while TfL insists it wants to avoid disruption and find a negotiated solution. The RMT has threatened strikes unless their demands are met, raising concerns about widespread disruption for London's transport network. If no agreement is reached, the dispute could lead to further Tube strikes, impacting millions of commuters and travelers across the city.

articles.title: Scientists discover 5.5 million bees living beneath a New York cemetery for over 100 years and it could help save vulnerable pollinators | - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Cornell University researchers discovered an estimated 5.5 million mining bees living in a hidden underground aggregation beneath East Lawn Cemetery in Ithaca, New York. The discovery highlights the importance of undisturbed habitats for pollinators and could provide valuable insights into conserving vulnerable bee populations facing threats from habitat loss, pesticides, and climate change.  The site may have existed since the early 1900s due to favorable nesting conditions and limited disturbance, offering a rare glimpse into how native bees can thrive in seemingly ordinary locations.

articles.title: Scientists found a hidden signal beneath the Sun and it may change what we know about solar cycles | - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: A team of scientists led by Professor William J. Chaplin from the University of Birmingham analyzed nearly four decades of data collected by the Birmingham Solar-Oscillations Network (BiSON), a global network that measures oscillations inside the Sun.  Their findings suggest that structural changes occurring in relation to Solar Cycles 22, 23, 24, and 25 are moving deeper into the outer layers of the solar core, indicating a hidden signal beneath the surface. This discovery challenges traditional methods of gauging solar activity by focusing on sunspots and radio flux, suggesting that the Sun's interior may be far more active than previously thought. The study also highlights the potential implications for future solar activity and space weather phenomena.

articles.title: A Maharashtra BJP pick for MLC polls with connection to Pawars: Who is Arun Lakhani? | Political Pulse News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: Arun Lakhani, a prominent Maharashtra BJP leader and close associate of Union Minister Nitin Gadkari and Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis, has been nominated to represent the Wardha-Chandrapur-Gadchiroli Local Authorities constituency in the upcoming June 18 state MLC elections.  Lakhani's nomination has sparked debate due to his lack of local roots within the constituency, but he is a familiar face within the party and known for his work in infrastructure development and social initiatives. His son, Sarang Lakhani, is engaged to NCP (SP) MP Supriya Sule’s daughter, Revati, further adding to the political intrigue surrounding his candidacy.

articles.title: Websites Can Now Spy on You Through Your Hard Drive | WIRED
articles.rephrased_article: Meta and Yandex were recently caught engaging in privacy-invasive tracking techniques, and now a new method called FROST has emerged. This technique exploits side channels on solid-state drives to monitor website activity and open applications on a visitor's device. The attack relies on measuring the timing of I/O operations within the OPFS (origin private file system) and uses a convolutional neural network to classify these traces, inferring user activity. While FROST requires no interaction from the visitor, its reliance on large OPFS files and limited applicability to devices using separate SSD drives for apps pose limitations.  However, researchers propose browser makers limit the size of such files and shut down the side channel.

articles.title: Can India's Delivery Workers Escape the Trap of Time-Bound Labour?
articles.rephrased_article: Delivery agents employed by food and grocery platforms in Delhi reported working over 84 hours a week to meet incentive thresholds, despite earning only between Rs 25,000 and Rs 30,000 per month. This practice reflects the pressure of time-bound labor within the competitive platform economy, which is built on maximizing profits through speed and constant availability.  The author argues that this exploitation mirrors historical forms of labor control, such as Taylorism and Fordism, and calls for greater protection for workers in this new digital landscape.

articles.title: France Tanker Seizure: ‘International terrorism’: Russia slams France's seizure of Russian-linked tanker, terms it 'illegal' - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Russia strongly condemned France's detention of a Russian-linked oil tanker, the Tagor, in the Atlantic Ocean, calling it illegal and bordering on international terrorism.  The Kremlin stated that the vessel was being used to circumvent Western sanctions imposed over the Ukraine war. French President Emmanuel Macron announced the seizure of the tanker, which departed from Murmansk and was heading towards Cameroon, with support from Britain and other partners. Authorities in France opened a criminal investigation into the vessel for failing to prove its nationality and refusing to comply with orders.

articles.title: Empty Stomach, Waiter Jobs: An Indian Student's Story Of The Falling Rupee
articles.rephrased_article: Divyam Sharma, an Indian student studying at King's College London, has experienced the impact of a weakening rupee on his daily life.  As the exchange rate between the rupee and pound fluctuates, Sharma highlights how it affects his tuition fees, monthly expenses, and overall financial well-being. He notes that while he is not alone in facing these challenges, the situation is particularly difficult for students who rely heavily on currency conversions. Despite the difficulties, Sharma emphasizes that living abroad has taught him valuable lessons about budgeting and appreciating the city's diverse experiences.

articles.title: The Romance Scammer Who Made a Small Fortune Posing as a WWE Superstar | WIRED
articles.rephrased_article: Carlos Barragán's book, "The Yahoo Boys: Love, Deception, and the Real Lives of Nigeria’s Romance Scammers," details Chibuike's journey from a desperate young man in Lagos to a sophisticated romance scammer.  Chibuike began by impersonating the world champion wrestler Cody Rhodes, using prewritten scripts and fabricated stories to convince a woman named Theresa he was the real deal. He skillfully manipulated her emotions and finances, convincing her to send him hundreds of euros through various excuses like "billing" for travel expenses, medical bills, and even gifts. Over four years, Chibuike scammed Theresa out of 78,000 euros, highlighting the devastating impact of online romance scams on vulnerable individuals.

articles.title: 'Stressed, Tired': Why Indian Employees Still Don't Use All Their Leaves
articles.rephrased_article: A new analysis by global payroll and HR platform Deel reveals that Indian employees, despite having generous leave entitlements compared to many Asia-Pacific countries, are among the least likely to use them fully. The data shows that only 17.2% of Indian workers exhausted their annual leave entitlement in 2025, with a median leave taken of just 12 days annually. This trend suggests that while employees may not be avoiding time off altogether, they are more selective about how they use it, often opting for shorter breaks.  Experts attribute this to workplace psychology and cultural factors such as the fear of appearing less committed or concerns about being perceived as replaceable. The analysis highlights the need for employers to address the underlying reasons behind underutilized leave, ensuring a culture that encourages employees to fully disconnect and recharge.

articles.title: Mango The Sweet Diplomat, From Mughals To Modern India
articles.rephrased_article: Americans are embracing Kesar mangoes, a popular Indian fruit, after a long-standing ban was lifted in 2006. This trend began with then President George Bush's appreciation for the fruit during a visit to India and has continued through subsequent years of diplomatic exchanges between the two countries.  The tradition of gifting mangoes dates back centuries, from Mughal emperors who used them as diplomatic tools to modern-day leaders like Prime Minister Narendra Modi who have received gifts of mangoes from other nations. The practice continues today with President Pranab Mukherjee, Sheikh Hasina, and others using mangoes as a symbol of goodwill between their countries.

articles.title: How India-Oman Trade Pact Opens Alternative Route To Gulf Beyond Hormuz
articles.rephrased_article: The India-Oman Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA) commenced today, offering zero-duty access to a wide range of Indian exports to Oman. This agreement comes amid disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz due to the US-Iran conflict, with Oman's strategic location providing an alternative trade and energy gateway for India.  Piyush Goyal, Union Commerce and Industry Minister, highlighted that this deal will boost exports, attract investments, and create jobs, while Ajay Srivastav, founder of Global Trade Research Initiative (GTRI), noted the agreement's significance in ensuring reliable trade even during geopolitical instability.

articles.title: ‘Sexual Chocolate’ Faces Recalls After FDA Tests Reveal Undisclosed Viagra | WIRED
articles.rephrased_article: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has issued several alerts regarding chocolate products marketed for “sexual enhancement” that contain undisclosed drugs, including sildenafil and tadalafil, the active ingredients in Viagra and Cialis.  The FDA advises consumers not to purchase these chocolates due to potential health risks, including interactions with nitrates found in prescription medications. Several brands, including Boner Bears Chocolate and Lovion Chocolate With Ginseng for Men, are being voluntarily recalled by distributors such as Nalpac and Gear Isle. The agency also warns that the products may interact with nitrates found in some prescription drugs, such as nitroglycerin, and may lower blood pressure to dangerous levels.

articles.title: Dead For Years, Active Before Attack: The Phone Trail Behind Pahalgam Attack
articles.rephrased_article: The National Investigation Agency (NIA) and the Jammu and Kashmir Police have uncovered evidence suggesting that a 2025 Pahalgam attack was planned for years. Investigations revealed that one of the two mobile phones used by terrorists in the attack was imported into Pakistan in 2021, financed by a Karachi-based bank previously linked to terrorism cases. The phone remained unused for four years before being activated just prior to the attack.  The investigation is now focusing on uncovering networks providing technical and logistical support from Pakistan.
articles.civic_flag_reason: The article suggests a long-planned attack financed by a known terrorist entity.

articles.title: A Bachelor's In Rare Earths? China Has Schools For That
articles.rephrased_article: China has established a robust education system for rare earths, with over 40 specialized labs and at least 11 universities enrolling more than 500 students annually in rare earth degree programs. This strong pipeline of talent sustains Beijing's dominance in global rare earth refining.  The US is lagging behind, with limited undergraduate degrees and low mining enrollments. Despite this, the US Department of Energy is investing in domestic mining expertise and international cooperation to bolster its rare earths capabilities.

articles.title: Iran war day 94: US strikes Iranian sites; Kuwait intercepts missiles | US-Israel war on Iran News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The United States military conducted "self-defense strikes" on Iranian radar and drone sites, while the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) retaliated by targeting a US base.  Iran has restored gas production at three offshore platforms after Israeli attacks in March. Meanwhile, President Donald Trump stated that Iran is eager to reach an agreement, calling it "a good one for the USA and those that are with us." The conflict escalated as Israel deepened its offensive into southern Lebanon, prompting Hezbollah to shoot down an Israeli drone.  The situation remains tense, with both sides exchanging messages on a potential deal.

articles.title: Washington proposes ‘roadmap’ for de-escalation in Lebanon: US official | News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The United States has proposed a "roadmap" for de-escalation in Lebanon, involving Hezbollah halting attacks on Israel in exchange for Israel refraining from further escalation in Beirut. However, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu ordered military operations in southern Lebanon's Dahiyeh district, claiming the capture of Beaufort Castle marks a "dramatic shift" in the campaign against Hezbollah.  The US official blamed Hezbollah for prolonging the conflict and accused Iran of manipulating it as a mediator. The escalation has resulted in widespread condemnation from countries like France, the United Kingdom, and Qatar, who have called for Israel to halt its military activities in Lebanon.

articles.title: Watch: Indian Ambassador Vikram Doraiswami Speaks Mandarin, Gives Tour Of Indian Embassy In Beijing
articles.rephrased_article: Vikram Doraiswami, India's Ambassador to China, is gaining attention for a video tour of the Indian Embassy in Beijing. In the video, Doraiswami speaks fluent Mandarin and introduces himself as "Wei Jiameng," highlighting cultural ties between India and China, referencing Rabindranath Tagore's visit to China over a century ago.  He also showcases various sections of the embassy, including its cultural center, where courses like yoga and dance are offered, and an exhibition area displaying handicrafts from across India.

articles.title: Vinicius brings Maracana curtain-raiser to life as Brazil rout Panama 6-2 | World Cup 2026 | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Brazil defeated Panama 6-2 in a friendly match, with Vinicius Jr. scoring two goals and setting up another.  The victory served as preparation for the upcoming World Cup, where Brazil will be without key players like Neymar. The game saw Carlo Ancelotti make significant changes to his starting lineup.  Christian Pulisic scored one goal and created another for Folarin Balogun in a 3-2 win against Senegal, as the USA prepared for their World Cup opener against Paraguay.

articles.title: Political commentators Cenk, Piker say UK bars them over Israel remarks | Israel-Palestine conflict News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Cenk Uygur and Hasan Piker, US political commentators, were denied entry to the UK due to their criticism of Israel.  They allege that British authorities cited their public comments about Israel as the reason for the decision, stating they pose a "serious risk" to public order. The pair also claim that their criticisms of Israel's influence on American politics are being labeled as antisemitic. The Times newspaper reported that UK officials stated Uygur’s presence was not “conducive to the public good.

articles.title: Iran’s IRGC launches retaliatory strike after US attacks | US-Israel war on Iran News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) of Iran launched a retaliatory strike on a US base in Kuwait after the US carried out strikes on Iran's communications tower. The attacks came as indirect negotiations between the US and Iran to formalize a fragile ceasefire continue, with reports suggesting mixed signals about whether an agreement will be reached.  The US Central Command (CENTCOM) stated that no US troops were hurt in the attacks, while Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesperson blamed "lack of trust" and contradictory positions from the US for delays in negotiations.

articles.title: Ethiopia election under way as Abiy Ahmed seeks another term but no voting in Tigray
articles.rephrased_article: The Ethiopian general election is underway, but conflict in parts of the country has prevented many from voting. The northern region of Tigray, which was ravaged by a brutal civil war ending in 2022, is excluded from the poll. Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed's Prosperity Party is expected to win, despite criticism over his government's suppression of dissent and human rights violations.  The election takes place amidst ongoing tensions with neighboring Eritrea and violent insurgencies in Amhara and Oromia regions, raising concerns about potential instability. Many young voters hope the election will bring stability, but some express apprehension about its impact on their lives.

articles.title: Donald Trump Mount Rushmore Moment? AI Photo Shows Him With 4 US Presidents George Washington, Thomas Jefferson, Theodore Roosevelt, Abraham Lincoln
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump shared an AI-generated image on Truth Social that depicts him alongside the faces of four presidents on Mount Rushmore. The post reignited discussions about his long-standing interest in being included on the iconic monument, a sentiment he has previously expressed publicly. Kristi Noem, South Dakota Governor, confirmed that Trump had mentioned his desire to be added to Mount Rushmore during an earlier meeting.  This renewed conversation follows previous public remarks by Trump expressing his interest and even joking about the possibility.

articles.title: Shibuya: Japan introduces litter fine in Tokyo's tourist hotspot
articles.rephrased_article: Tokyo's Shibuya Ward has implemented on-the-spot fines of 2,000 Japanese yen for littering in an effort to curb the growing issue. The new penalties, part of a broader anti-littering campaign, aim to address concerns about public cleanliness and tourism impact. Authorities will deploy up to 50 officials to enforce the fines, which can be paid via cash, credit card, or QR codes. This initiative follows a surge in tourism following the Covid pandemic, leading to challenges for local communities and infrastructure.

articles.title: France intercepts sanctioned Russian oil tanker, Macron says
articles.rephrased_article: Emmanuel Macron announced that France seized a sanctioned Russian oil tanker, the Tagor, with UK support in international waters. The French Navy boarded the vessel after it was found to be flying a false flag and violating international sanctions on Russia's oil exports.  The Kremlin condemned the seizure as "bordering on international piracy" while the UK Prime Minister Sir Keir Starmer previously granted permission for UK military involvement in intercepting sanctioned Russian ships.

articles.title: Ebola outbreak: DR Congo celebrates recovery of five nurses
articles.rephrased_article: The World Health Organization (WHO) and the Democratic Republic of Congo's Institute of Public Health are celebrating the recovery of five Ebola patients from a hospital in Bunia, the epicenter of the outbreak.  These recoveries mark an encouraging milestone and highlight the effectiveness of early detection, medical care, contact tracing, and community engagement. Dr Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, WHO chief, emphasized the importance of community collaboration and trust for successful response efforts. The current outbreak has caused over 246 deaths in the Democratic Republic of Congo and neighboring Uganda.

articles.title: Tirumala Sees Record Surge In Hair Offerings, 1.24 Million Devotees Shave Heads
articles.rephrased_article: Tirumala Tirupati Devasthanams (TTD), which manages the world's richest Hindu shrine, recorded over 12.43 lakh hair offerings from devotees in May 2024, surpassing previous years and reaching a peak of 57,580 daily tonsuring on May 23rd. The increase is attributed to summer holidays, weekend rush, and pilgrims from across India and abroad. To handle the high demand, TTD has maintained round-the-clock tonsuring services with over 1,150 barbers working in shifts.  The hair collected is auctioned for use in wig, hair extension, and beauty industries, generating significant revenue for TTD.

articles.title: Tiger Shroff ‘smells’ cake but won’t take a bite, says sis Krishna; expert on extreme discipline | Fitness News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: Krishna Shroff, sister of actor Tiger Shroff, shared insights into her brother's disciplined approach to fitness.  She revealed that Tiger Shroff is extremely focused on training and avoids late-night cravings, prioritizing sleep and structured eating habits. Psychologist Rasshi Gurnani explained that while discipline is crucial for achieving fitness goals, an overly rigid approach can be detrimental, leading to anxiety, guilt, and unhealthy relationships with food and exercise.  Gurnani suggests a more balanced perspective where food and movement are viewed as sources of nourishment and pleasure rather than tools for punishment or control.

articles.title: Israel PM orders strikes on Beirut suburbs as Hezbollah conflict escalates
articles.rephrased_article: Benjamin Netanyahu, the Israeli prime minister, ordered strikes on the southern Beirut suburbs in response to attacks on Israeli civilians and violations of a US-brokered ceasefire. Marco Rubio, the US Secretary of State, urged both sides to cease hostilities and pressure Hezbollah to stop its attacks on Israel. Joseph Aoun, the Lebanese president, is relying on US mediation efforts to prevent further civilian casualties. The conflict escalated after Hezbollah launched rockets into Israel in retaliation for an Israeli strike that killed Iran's supreme leader.

articles.title: France Tanker Seizure: ‘International terrorism’: Russia slams France's seizure of Russian-linked tanker, terms it 'illegal' - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Russia strongly condemned France's detention of the oil tanker Tagor, calling it illegal and bordering on international terrorism. The Kremlin stated that the vessel was suspected of being part of Russia's "shadow fleet" used to circumvent Western sanctions imposed over the Ukraine war. France has opened a criminal investigation into the vessel for failing to prove its nationality, refusing to comply with authorities, and sailing under a suspected false Cameroonian flag.

articles.title: Iran attacks damage 20 US military sites since start of war, satellite images show
articles.rephrased_article: Iran has damaged 20 US military sites since the start of the war, according to satellite imagery analysis by BBC Verify.  The attacks have targeted key facilities across eight countries in the Middle East, causing millions of dollars worth of damage to state-of-the-art air defense systems, refuelling aircraft and radars. The Pentagon has reported destroying over 13,000 targets in Iran, but analysts suggest that Tehran's counter-attacks have been more precise and extensive than previously acknowledged.  The US is seeking to limit satellite analysis of the conflict by requesting Planet, a major provider, to impose an "indefinite" restriction on new images of Iran and most of the Middle East.

articles.title: US, Iran trade new attacks amid talks: Here’s what we know | US-Israel war on Iran News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The US and Iran have continued to exchange attacks despite a ceasefire that began on April 8. The US military struck Iranian radar and drone sites over the weekend, while Iran retaliated by targeting a US base in the Gulf region.  Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) has also claimed responsibility for attacks on Kuwait, Saudi Arabia, and the UAE. Donald Trump claims he is close to achieving a "very good deal" with Iran but negotiations have been strained by recent attacks. The Iranian government maintains that it will not agree to any deal that does not secure full Iranian rights.

articles.title: Japan-Philippines Maritime Talks: China patrols east Taiwan waters ahead of Japan-Philippines maritime delimitation talks - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: China’s coast guard conducted patrols in waters east of Taiwan in response to Japan and the Philippines announcing maritime boundary delimitation talks.  The Chinese government asserts that these waters are under its sovereignty, while Taiwan rejects this claim and insists on its own territorial rights. Beijing has previously expressed disapproval of such discussions and urged Japan and the Philippines to cease any actions that infringe upon China's sovereign rights.

articles.title: Nearly 60 out of 80 TMC MLAs skip Mamata meeting, party blames attack on its MPs | Kolkata News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: TMC postponed a meeting with newly elected MLAs after most failed to attend due to ongoing protests and police action following attacks on party leaders.  The party's spokesperson, Kunal Ghosh, stated that the meeting was postponed until later date as the MLAs were assisting arrested party workers. Mamata Banerjee will lead a protest rally in Kolkata on June 1st against the attacks on her nephew, Abhishek Banerjee, and other party members.

articles.title: Eating oats every day? A dietitian reveals mistakes that could cancel their benefits | Health and Wellness News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: Dr. Archana Batra, a clinical dietician, advises against consuming oats as the sole meal component and emphasizes incorporating them into balanced breakfasts. Dr. Batra suggests adding protein sources like yogurt, nuts, or seeds to oatmeal for increased satiety and sustained energy levels.  She cautions against using oat milk as a nutritional replacement for dairy milk due to its low protein content and added ingredients that can alter the nutritional profile.

articles.title: Stalin Wine Cellar: Inside Stalin’s hidden wine cellar in Georgia: 40,000 rare French and Georgian bottles emerge after decades underground | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Georgian authorities opened a secret wine cellar containing approximately 40,000 bottles of rare French and Georgian wines to the public. The collection, believed to date back more than 200 years, was assembled by Josef Stalin, who took an interest in wine during his rule over the Soviet Union.  The government plans to auction parts of the cellar to establish a wine education school, hoping to boost Georgia's international wine market profile. The collection is shrouded in historical intrigue due to Stalin's controversial legacy and the wines' connection to imperial Russia.

articles.title: RCB win IPL: Virat Kohli, Krunal Pandya dance to dhol beats
articles.rephrased_article: The Royal Challengers Bengaluru (RCB) won the IPL final against the Gujarat Titans, securing their second consecutive title.  Virat Kohli and his wife, Anushka Sharma, were seen thanking fans at the stadium, while Krunal Pandya and other players danced in celebration. The team joins Chennai Super Kings and Mumbai Indians as the only franchises to achieve back-to-back IPL titles.

articles.rephrased_article: A group of individuals, including Prajwal Ashok Teli, Praj Rajendra Patil, and Chandraprakash Phoolchand, were arrested for hacking CCTV systems at hospitals, malls, and commercial buildings across India. articles.rephrased_article: The B.Ed Joint Entrance Examination (JEE) 2026 was successfully conducted in Uttar Pradesh on Sunday, with 90% of the 4,44,958 registered candidates participating. articles.title: 10 darkest regions on Earth where you can get the clearest views of planets, stars and the Milky Way | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: The Atacama Desert in Chile, the Namib Desert in Namibia, and other locations around the world offer exceptional night-sky conditions for stargazing. These regions are characterized by low population density, minimal light pollution, and high altitudes, creating clear views of celestial objects like planets, constellations, and the Milky Way.  These dark skies are crucial for scientific research and provide a valuable opportunity for people to connect with the natural world.

articles.title: Commercial LPG Prices Hiked By Rs 42 In Delhi, Rs 53.5 In Kolkata Amid Iran war
articles.rephrased_article: Commercial LPG prices in Delhi rose by Rs 42 to Rs 3,113.50 per cylinder from June 1st, marking a nearly doubling of costs since January. This increase follows a series of price hikes throughout the year, driven by disruptions in global energy supply chains due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East and tensions around the Gulf region. The rise in LPG prices has also impacted CNG prices, which have increased by Rs 2 per kg.  The government is working to build larger reserves of LPG to mitigate future disruptions and strengthen India's energy security. This will likely impact businesses and consumers as they face higher cooking costs and potential price increases for meals, services, and products.

articles.title: Weather Today LIVE Updates | IMD Weather Forecast Delhi NCR, UP, Noida, Rajasthan Heatwave Updates: Drastic Drop In Temperatures Keeps Delhi Cool
articles.rephrased_article: India Meteorological Department (IMD) forecasts continued relief from the summer heat in Delhi-NCR as rain and thunderstorms are expected until June 4th.  The IMD also predicts scattered rainfall and gusty winds across the region, keeping daytime temperatures below 40 degrees Celsius through at least June 6th. Heavy rainfall is anticipated in Uttar Pradesh, Rajasthan, and southern states as the monsoon progresses.

articles.title: Noida Trekker Goes Missing On Uttarakhand's Pindari Glacier Trail, Search On
articles.rephrased_article: State Disaster Response Force (SDRF) teams are searching for missing trekker Vishesh Chauhan in Uttarakhand's Bageshwar district after he separated from his local porter on the Pindari Glacier route.  Chauhan, who was returning from the trek, failed to reach the base by the scheduled time and prompted a request for SDRF assistance. The team used rope rescue techniques to search a suspected location but Chauhan remains missing.

articles.title: Nepal has encroached on Indian territory as well: PM Balendra Shah - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Nepal Prime Minister Balendra Shah sparked a political uproar in Parliament after his comments about border encroachment. The government later clarified that the remarks were due to technical factors related to shifting river boundaries.

articles.title: Iran-US war, What To Know As Israel's Lebanon Incursion In 25 Years Complicates Iran Deal
articles.rephrased_article: Israel seized the symbolic Beaufort fort in southern Lebanon, a move that challenges a US-brokered ceasefire and raises concerns from Qatar, Germany, and other countries.
